summary: Canaima Airport (CAJ) serves the small indigenous community of Canaima in Venezuela's Bolívar State, acting as the primary gateway to Canaima National Park and the world-famous Angel Falls. The airport features a single asphalt runway and handles mostly domestic tourist and charter flights, as the region is largely inaccessible by road. Its remote jungle location makes it one of the most scenically situated airports in South America.
faqs:
Q: How do I get from Canaima Airport to Angel Falls?
A: Most visitors book package tours that include a flight or boat transfer from the airport to the falls, as the falls are deep within the national park and require guided transport.

Q: Are there flights from Caracas to Canaima Airport?
A: Yes, several Venezuelan carriers operate domestic flights from Caracas to Canaima, typically on smaller aircraft suited to the short runway.

Q: What facilities are available at Canaima Airport?
A: The airport has very basic facilities including a small terminal building, as it primarily serves the local community and park visitors rather than commercial traffic.

Q: Is Canaima Airport served by international flights?
A: No, Canaima Airport only handles domestic flights within Venezuela, as it is a small regional airport in a remote area.
transport_tips: Arrange ground transport and tour packages in advance, as the airport is remote and taxis or local guides are the main options for onward travel. The nearby Laguna de Canaima is reachable on foot from the airport, and most lodges offer pickup services. Expect small turboprop aircraft on most flights, as the runway limits the size of planes that can land there.
local_tip: Pack light and bring a waterproof bag, as weather in the Canaima region can change rapidly and the lagoon area is frequently misty even when the airport area is clear.
